source.title: Muon: Training and Trade-offs with Latent Attention and MoE
source.authors: Sushant Mehta; R. Dandekar; R. Dandekar; Sreedath Panat

record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer configurations and reports validation perplexity and loss, but does not measure the training-to-test generalization gap or test any listed version directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation performance for Muon and AdamW and for several architecture combinations. It does not report training error alongside held-out error, random-label fitting, or the effects named in the claim versions. Cited results from other work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study compares Muon, AdamW and architectural variants for language-model efficiency. It does not establish any listed version: the batch comparisons lack a fixed epoch or token budget, and the optimizer experiments do not establish a standard SGD comparison under the tuning conditions named in V4. Missing training-to-test gaps alone would not exclude V4 or V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase broadly matches the authors' conclusions: Muon reduces compute to target loss, preserves relative data efficiency at large batches, and combines with MLA and MoE for efficiency gains. They do not conclude anything about a training-to-test generalization gap. Their claimed 68% memory reduction is not substantiated by the peak-memory values in Table 3.
record.recipe_differences: Small and medium decoder-only Transformer training; compares Muon with AdamW and architectural variants, not the interventions or measurements in the listed original studies.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports optimizer, model-scale, batch-size, and architecture comparisons, but does not measure their effects on the claimed training-to-test gap.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 2 reports validation perplexity of 8.462 for Muon and 8.579 for AdamW. Table 3 likewise reports lower final perplexity for Muon within each architecture, although its evaluation split is unspecified.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Muon achieves lower reported final perplexity than AdamW in the tested language-model configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 3 reports small perplexity increases when replacing MHA with MLA, and larger decreases when adding MoE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention compression and conditional computation change final perplexity in these language models.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 2 reports validation perplexities of 8.485, 8.465 and 8.470 at batches of 0.5M, 2M and 8M tokens, respectively, but does not establish equal training budgets. Figure 2 measures tokens needed to reach target losses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Muon maintains similar reported validation perplexity across these batch configurations and retains a token-efficiency advantage over AdamW at large batches.

fits_no_version.finding: The momentum-only ablation reports validation perplexity 8.521 versus AdamW's 8.579, but its precise update, tuning and matched training budget are insufficiently specified.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing orthogonalization yields a momentum-only variant with lower reported validation perplexity than the AdamW baseline in this ablation.

record.problems: The reported final perplexities are not explicitly identified as test metrics in the supplied text, and no corresponding training errors or uncertainty estimates are given. Several results are figures without extractable numerical values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows extracted. Table 2 ablations report other Muon-specific components, and Figure 1 reports validation-loss curves without numerical values; neither establishes the claimed generalization gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting alongside natural-label and random-label held-out performance.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.

Adaptive methods versus standard SGD or momentum SGD under characterized tuning conditions, including the specified recovery mechanisms. The momentum-only ablation does not document a matched standard momentum-SGD recipe or tuning protocol.
Held-out performance across batch sizes at a fixed epoch or token budget, and whether recipe adaptations remove a penalty.
Dropout's effects and its interactions with dataset size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness tracking generalization gaps. Spectral normalization of optimizer updates does not measure this.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's proposed architecture-dependent direction of the Muon–AdamW perplexity difference is incorrect: Muon has lower reported perplexity within all three architectures. The training dataset, complete tuning protocol, evaluation split for Table 3 and uncertainty estimates are unspecified.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under limited tuning; recovery by broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching, or language-model results.
Large-batch effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and the listed recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on held-out error and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures tracking the training-to-test gap.
Effects of removing memorized training examples on held-out accuracy.
